title: Optional: the headless server starts, makes a certificate and a token
covers: apps/desktop/server: archipelia-server start through the server launch target
context: The server target runs the same lobby server without a window. On first start it makes a self signed certificate, prints its fingerprint, listens and writes an admin token. This is a cheap check before the test of remote servers, which needs it running.

setup.label: terminal
setup.text: PowerShell at X:\archipelia. The run line sets three settings for this terminal only, then starts the server from the bundle-4 worktree.

setup.label: data folder
setup.text: The server uses the data folder of the bundle-4 worktree (.user-data). Do not run the bundle-4 desktop app at the same time.

setup.label: port
setup.text: The run line uses port 38390 on 127.0.0.1 only, so no firewall alert and no clash with the desktop app on 38290.

run: $env:ARCHIPELIA_PORT='38390'; $env:ARCHIPELIA_LOOPBACK='true'; $env:ARCHIPELIA_ENGINE_AUTO='false'; archipelia worktree launch bundle-4 none --target server
steps: Paste the run line in the terminal and press Enter. Leave the terminal open.
Read the log. A line says no configuration file: the defaults and the environment apply.
A line reads TLS generated: SHA-256 fingerprint, followed by a long hex value.
A line starts with lobby server on wss:// and ends with port 38390 and a network mode.
In File Explorer open .user-data\Data\server of the bundle-4 worktree. A file admin-token exists and holds a long text.
Run the test Archipelia servers now. It finds this server and shows the same fingerprint.
Stop the server with Ctrl+C when you are done. The log ends without an error.
pass: The server starts, prints a fingerprint, listens on wss and writes an admin token.
The fingerprint printed here is the one the desktop shows when it first trusts the server.
fail: The server exits at once, prints an error, or listens on the wrong address.
No token file is written, or the fingerprint differs from the desktop.
notes: OPTIONAL. Skip it if you do not test the remote server.
Not covered: docker/compose.yaml. Its README says it has not been run on a Docker host yet.
Windows is not the usual host for this server. If it fails to start on Windows, note the log and skip.
